title: Security review process for enterprise deals (questionnaires, artifacts, approvals)
author: Aisha Rahman
content:
## Purpose
This page documents the security/compliance steps in the **end-to-end process for getting a non-standard enterprise deal approved and signed at Redwood Inference**. It is intended for AEs, Solutions Engineering, and Security.

Security review is a gate for many enterprise customers and must be tracked explicitly to avoid last-minute blockers.

## When a security review is required
Security review is required when any of the following applies:
- Customer requests a security questionnaire (SIG, CAIQ, custom spreadsheets)
- Customer requests SOC 2, ISO statements, pen test letters, or security architecture
- Customer requires a DPA, data residency commitment, or custom audit language
- Customer is evaluating **Dedicated** or **Private** deployments (common for regulated workloads)

## Roles
- **AE:** owns customer timeline and ensures intake form fields are complete.
- **Solutions Engineer (SE):** supports technical questions; does not commit to security features outside approved statements.
- **Security:** owns responses, approves security exhibits, and signs off on security commitments.
- **Legal:** owns contract language; coordinates with Security on security addenda.

## Required inputs (must be provided in the Deal Intake Form)
- Customer legal entity name
- Deployment mode (Hosted, Dedicated, Private)
- Requested regions and any data residency constraints
- Whether customer requires: DPA, SLA addendum, custom audit rights
- Due date for questionnaire

## Standard artifacts (what we provide)
- Redwood SOC 2 Type II report (under NDA where required)
- Security overview (hosted + dedicated + private high-level controls)
- Subprocessor list and notification policy (standard)
- Incident response summary (high-level)

## Questionnaire handling procedure
1) AE opens a Security intake ticket and links the Deal Intake Form + customer questionnaire.
2) Security assigns an owner and target response date.
3) Security completes responses using the approved control statements library.
4) Any question that implies a contractual commitment is flagged to Legal.
5) AE sends the completed questionnaire to the customer and records the version sent in the CRM record.

## What requires Security sign-off (explicit)
Security must explicitly sign off before signature if the deal includes any of:
- Customer-specific security exhibit
- Custom audit rights language
- Data residency commitment beyond standard regions
- On-prem / air-gapped packaging commitments
- Non-standard retention/deletion timelines

## What Sales/SE must NOT do
- Do not provide internal diagrams, runbooks, or unreleased architecture docs.
- Do not commit to fixed breach notification windows or audit procedures; route to Legal.
- Do not claim certifications we do not hold.

## Exit criteria (security gate complete)
Security gate is complete when:
- Security marks the intake ticket as "Approved" (or "Approved with Conditions")
- Any conditions are either reflected in contract language (Legal) or removed from scope

## Notes for non-standard enterprise deal process
Security completion does not imply pricing or legal approval. All three gates (pricing, legal, security) must be complete prior to sending for final signature.
